name: Easter long weekend - Paradise and Long Beaches, Cape Cleveland
description:
Easter long weekend overnighter - Cape Cleveland to Paradise and Bedwell Bay

When: Friday 3 April - Sunday 5 April (Easter long weekend)
Location: Cape Cleveland, Bowling Green Bay National Park
Leader: Wilfred
Grade: Intermediate
Expressions of Interest: Contact Wilfred wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com.au

Wilfred is leading a two-night Easter overnighter to one of North Queensland’s classic coastal wilderness routes. The plan is to walk from Cape Cleveland out to Paradise Beach on Friday, camping near the freshwater creek. On Saturday, the group will traverse from Paradise Beach up to the saddle, across to Long Beach (Bedwell Bay), returning via Castle Rock for expansive views over the rugged coastline before heading back to camp. Sunday will be the walk out the same way we came in.

This is a remote, self-sufficient coastal bushwalk through semi-evergreen rainforest, coastal forest and exposed beach sections. Expect off-track navigation, uneven terrain, sand walking and warm conditions. Participants should be comfortable carrying an overnight pack and walking for several hours each day.

Water is available at the Paradise Beach creek, so you will only need to carry sufficient water for each day’s walking. All other food, camping gear and essentials must be carried in.

This is a beautiful and committing Easter adventure - remote beaches, granite headlands, star-filled skies and the kind of coastline most people in Townsville never see. Expressions of interest are now open.

name: The Original Scramble Track
description:
When: 10th April 2026
Location: Castle Hill, Townsville
Leader: Luen
Grade: 4
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

Step off the better-known Castle Hill paths and explore one of the hill's older, rougher, and more mysterious lines to the summit. This hike follows what is thought to be one of the original routes up Castle Hill - a historical track that appears in aerial imagery from the 1950s and is known by several names, including The Cleft Track, The Crack Track, or simply "THE Track".

We will begin on the Cudtheringa Track and leave the main trail between the Eastern and Western Bluffs, heading into the gully that once formed this direct old route to the top. The track follows an intermittent creek line, with faded white-painted arrows still marking parts of the way. Along the route, we will pass the rock climbing crag called "Alias" and an old rusty ladder - a relic from a time when this section would likely have been climbed as a scramble - before continuing steeply upward to emerge near one of the Pillar Box Walk lookouts.

This is a short but steep, rough, and adventurous climb with a strong historical feel. Expect loose terrain, rocky footing, and some hands-on movement. Although the route itself is no longer maintained as a trail and was closed, this outing is for experienced walkers who are comfortable on steep off-track terrain and interested in Castle Hill's lesser-known past.

Bring:
- At least 1 L of water, optional as there's water at the top
- Sturdy walking shoes with good grip
- Hat and sun protection (optional)
- A small snack (optional)
- A small first aid kit
- Gloves optional, but handy for rough sections

This walk is suited to confident, sure-footed hikers with a reasonable level of fitness. It is not suitable for beginners, children, or anyone uncomfortable with steep, unstable terrain.

name: Little Birthday to Big Birthday - creek adventure
description:
Little Birthday to Big Birthday - creek adventure
When: Saturday 11 April 2026
Location: Mt Spec area, Paluma Range National Park
Leader: Luen
Duration: ~3-4 hours
Grade: 4, Moderate
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

Intro walk: Suitable for beginners with a good level of fitness. 

We are heading back into the rainforest for a quarter-day off-track creek adventure linking Little Birthday Creek to Big Birthday Creek in the Mt Spec area. This is a remote wilderness bushwalk with sustained creek walking, rock hopping, slippery granite, tangled vines and the usual North Queensland surprises underfoot. Expect to be in and out of the water for much of the day.

The plan is to explore upstream and downstream sections of the Birthday Creek system, navigating through cool rainforest corridors and sculpted creek lines. These walks are about immersion - moving through water, negotiating boulders, making route decisions on the go and enjoying pockets of pristine Paluma that most people never see.

If time allows, we'll head up to Torstens Rock Garden and explore around a bit more.

This is rated moderate. Participants must have solid fitness and be comfortable with 4 hours on foot in off-track terrain - think slippery rainforest creek rocks and swimming. Waterproof everything - phone, keys, food. Sturdy enclosed footwear with good grip is essential. Long sleeves recommended, gaiters optional.

Bring at least 2 L of water (or treat creek water if refilling), half-day food, electrolytes, a personal first-aid kit, a head torch, and a whistle.

Meeting details will be emailed to those who RSVP. If conditions are unsuitable, the route may be modified at the leader’s discretion.

Rainforest creeks, slippery rocks and character-building fun - this is Paluma at its best.

name: Mt Stuart Road fitness walk
description:
Mt Stuart Road fitness walk - Tuesday mornings
Date: 14 April 2026
When: Tuesdays, 4:45 am
Location: Mt Stuart Road, Townsville
Leaders: Wilfred
Grade: Low-Intermediate fitness
RSVP: wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com.au
The meeting location will be sent to those who RSVP.

Wilfred's regular Tuesday Mt Stuart road walk is open to club members who want a solid pre-dawn fitness hit. We will meet at 4:45 am and walk the bitumen road all the way to the 584 m summit and back, covering approximately 15 km return. This is a self-paced, steady uphill grind followed by a controlled descent - ideal for building endurance and leg strength. We walk up for 1.5 hours, which usually means we rest at the top and then go back down again ~1.5 hours.

As usual, we will bring a small bag and pick up rubbish along the way, giving the mountain a bit of care while we train. Bring water and a head torch, and be prepared for exposed conditions once the sun rises. No frills, just consistent effort, good company and sunrise views over Gurrumbilbarra.

name: Top of Jourama Falls - swim and picnic walk
description:
RSVP accepted via this platform - ❌
RSVP via email to walk leader directly - ✅👍
Please Note: Selecting Going on Facebook Events does not automatically register you for this event. Please contact the leader directly at brentgc1306@gmail.com (Brent) to secure your spot on this TBWC hike. This is important due diligence for our club insurance.

Top of Jourama Falls - swim and picnic walk
When: Sunday 26th April 7:00 am
Location: Jourama Falls, Paluma Range National Park
Leader: Brent
Grade: 3-4 (open to all levels - steep climb section)
RSVP: brentgc1306@gmail.com

Brent will be leading a relaxed but adventurous day out to the top of Jourama Falls, with a swim and picnic as the main focus. The plan is to walk in via the lookout track, tackle the steady ~10-minute climb from the lookout, and then another ~50 min to the top of the falls. It is a steep and often hot ascent, so a reasonable level of fitness and comfort on hills is important.

At the top, we will enjoy time around the pools and cascades - perfect for a swim, a long lunch and soaking in the granite scenery. If conditions are safe and time allows, Brent may explore a little further upstream along Waterview Creek, using the map as a guide and testing out some hands-on navigation.

This walk is open to all levels, but be prepared for heat, a sustained climb and uneven ground. Take your time, carry plenty of water and expect a social, exploratory day rather than a fast-paced mission.

Bring:
- At least 2-3 L of water
- Lunch and snacks
- Swimmers and towel
- Sturdy footwear with good grip
- Hat and sun protection

Meeting details will be provided once you RSVP directly to Brent.

A classic North Queensland combination: climb, cool off, eat well, repeat.
